title: DESIRE MS: A prospective randomized non-inferiority trial comparing anti-CD20 maintenance versus De-Escalation Strategy In Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis
official: DESIRE MS: A prospective randomized non-inferiority trial comparing anti-CD20 maintenance versus De-Escalation Strategy In Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis
summary: Main objective: To demonstrate the non-inferiority of de-escalation strategy from anti-CD20 therapy to platform therapies versus anti-CD20 maintenance in relapsing remitting MS patients on the % of patients without clinical and/or MRI disease activity between D0 and M36.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients ≥40 years at inclusion
2. Patients with relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis at inclusion (according to 2017 McDonald criteria) treated with anti-CD20 for at least the last 3 years. For patients treated with IV ocrelizumab or rituximab at extended interval dosing, a maximum interval of 12 months between perfusions during the year before inclusion visit is required
3. No evidence of disease activity for the last 3 years on anti-CD20 (No relapse AND no new/enlarged MRI lesion)
4. Brain MRI performed according to OFSEP protocol within a maximum of 6 months before randomization
Exclusion criteria:
1. Secondary or primary progressive MS at inclusion
2. Significantly impaired bone marrow function or significant anaemia, leukopenia, neutropenia or thrombocytopenia
3. Severe renal impairment undergoing dialysis
4. Severe hypoproteinaemia
5. Current severe depression and/or suicidal ideation
6. Suspected or confirmed progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML)
7. Any condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would interfere with the interpretation of patient safety or place the patient at high risk for treatment-related complications
8. Participation in another therapeutic trial in the last 6 months
9. Protected population according to articles of the French Public Health Code (e.g. patients under law protection, prisoners, pregnant, parturient or lactating women, and patients under guardianship/curatorship)
10. All women of childbearing age not using effective contraception during the study
11. Subjects not covered by public health insurance
12. Previous experience of treatment failure in patients treated with natalizumab, fingolimod, rituximab, ocrelizumab, mitoxantrone, alemtuzumab or cladribine
13. Failure to obtain written informed consent after a reflection period
14. Treatment with high dose corticosteroids during the 30 days preceding inclusion
15. Contraindication to MRI
16. Severely immunocompromised state
17. Current severe active infection
18. Known active malignancy
19. Severe heart failure (New York Heart Association Class IV) or severe, uncontrolled cardiac disease
20. Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C)
